newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants Central Africa mission to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: France wants Central Africa mission to go ahead.

text.p: France said on Monday a Canadian-led multinational mission to Zaire should go ahead despite the return of many refugees to Rwanda.
The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said earlier on Monday that half a million Hutu refugees had now crossed back into Rwanda from Zaire.

"The return of the refugees is encouraging news but this crisis has not been resolved. To end it, there must be a global approach, especially with the holding of a conference on the Great Lakes region," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.
Rummelhardt said there were still refugees in the region of Bukavu on the south of Lake Kivu and as a result "the force's mission must continue."
The UNCHR said it had no reports of any movement by some 500,000 refugees in the Bukavu area.
"We welcome the cooperation of Rwandan government authorities who, in concert with humanitarian organisations, work to receive these refugees in apparently satisfactory conditions," Rummelhardt said.
The refugees, Hutus who fled the arrival in power of a Tutsi-led movement in 1994, began returing last week after Zairean rebels forced Hutu fighters to flee to the hills.

Rummelhardt said France's Xavier Emmanuelli, secretary of state for emergency humanitarian action, was in the Rwandan capital Kigali where he had met officials and would travel to Kinshasa later on Monday.
Rummelhardt said the talks took place "in a positive atmosphere."

Rwanda's predominantly Tutsi government accuses France of being partisan after it sent troops to Rwanda in 1994 to help stop Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis and moderate Hutus. It charges that Paris used the intervention to help protect Hutus responsible for instigating the mass killings.

Countries planning to contribute troops to the mission were due to meet in Stuttgart on Wednesday to review the force's size and mandate following the refugees' return, a U.S. military official in Germany said.
French defence officials said last week they could have 600 soldiers in place within 24 hours of U.N. approval and another 600 troops within the next 24 hours.
